messages:
maria: Hey, publish for @redwood-sdk failed on CI — looks like regen-diffs flagged a semver mismatch so npm publish didn't run :facepalm:
kevin: Ugh, I saw the job. Which check exactly failed? regen-diffs or changelog-format?
jess: regen-diffs. The logs show a changed client file but package.json version wasn't bumped. CI refused to publish.
bot-ci: [regen-diffs] FAILED — files changed after codegen: src/clients/openapi-client.ts
bot-ci: Suggested command: yarn regen:openapi && git diff --name-only | cat
maria: Here's the failing snippet from the job output:
```
Error: Detected changes after code generation.
Files modified: src/clients/openapi-client.ts
Reason: generated client updated but package.json version unchanged
Action: bump version or commit generated changes
```
kevin: That usually means someone updated OpenAPI spec with a doc tweak and our typegen bumped the client formatting. Semver policy requires a patch bump for any generated client change.
tyler: Are we missing an automated step to auto-bump patch on regen-only diffs? I thought release-bot did that for some repos.
release-bot: publish workflow aborted: no version bump detected. If this was intended, run `yarn regen:openapi && npm version patch && git push && hub create-release`
jess: The trouble is we intentionally don't want to auto-bump for docs-only spec changes, but regen diffs can't easily tell doc-only vs behavior change. We need a safe policy.
maria: Immediate unblock: someone can regen locally, inspect diff, commit the generated file and run `npm version patch` in the package dir. I'll do it if someone approves.
kevin: I can verify quickly. Running locally now: `yarn regen:openapi && git add -A && git commit -m "chore(openapi): regen client" && npm version patch --no-git-tag-version`
tyler: Small nit — our publish job expects the git tag to be present. Use `npm version patch` (which creates tag) or ensure release-bot creates release from changelog.
jess: Also CI flagged our changelog-format linter in another PR — we should standardize on conventional commits so standard-version can generate changelogs predictably.
maria: +1. Right now some PRs use `fix:` others just `chore:` and that breaks auto-changelog heuristics.
kevin: Quick repro steps in case someone else hits this:
1) checkout the PR branch
2) `yarn regen:openapi`
3) `git diff --name-only` -> if any generated files appear, either commit them or revert the spec change
4) bump version with `npm version patch` and push

maria: I'm going to push a small fix: commit regen + patch bump. Tagging @kevin to review before I push.
kevin: Review done, looks fine. please add a short changelog entry in CHANGELOG.md to satisfy release-drafter.
release-bot: Note: if you include a header like `### Fixes` with a brief line, the release drafter will pick it up.
tyler: Longer-term: can we add a check that distinguishes whitespace/formatting-only changes in generated files? If regen changes only formatting, auto-patch. If models/endpoint signature changed, require manual review.
jess: That requires more heuristics but feasible — compare AST or use strict diff thresholds. Might be risky for the first pass.
maria: For now I'll push the manual fix so the publish can go through. Follow-up issue: create a task to explore auto-bump heuristics and enforce conventional commits for SDK repos.
kevin: Filed DEVEX-482: 'regen-diff autopatcher and semver heuristics' — assign to me and jess.
maria: Pushed the commit and bumped patch. CI retriggered.
bot-ci: [publish-job] queued...
bot-ci: [publish-job] SUCCESS — npm package redwood-sdk@1.2.3 published
maria: Published. Thanks all. Filing a short retro note on the PR about making the regen step clearer in the contributing guide. :tada:
